cards.design_implication: If the research design targets data from this specific observational window, it should align its scope with the compact binary coalescence events detected during O3a by LIGO and Virgo.
cards.evidence_excerpt: We report on gravitational wave discoveries from compact binary coalescences detected by Advanced LIGO and Advanced Virgo in the first half of the third observing run (O3a) between 1 April 2019 15:00 UTC and 1 October 2019 15:00 UTC.
limitations: This claim establishes the temporal and instrumental scope of the report but does not define specific sampling criteria for the events themselves.
cards.statement: The study analyzes gravitational wave discoveries from compact binary coalescences detected by Advanced LIGO and Advanced Virgo during the first half of the third observing run (O3a), specifically between 1 April 2019 15:00 UTC and 1 October 2019 15:00 UTC.

cards.design_implication: The design should consider a threshold-based selection for candidate events, noting that this specific threshold yields an expected contamination fraction of less than 10% based on the pipeline configuration.
does_not_establish: The specific implementation of the search algorithms
A causal link between thresholding and physical properties of the events
cards.evidence_excerpt: By imposing a false-alarm-rate threshold of two per year in each of the four search pipelines that constitute our search, we present 39 candidate gravitational wave events. At this threshold, we expect a contamination fraction of less than 10%.
limitations: This applies specifically to the four search pipelines used in this study.
It reflects the expectation for this dataset and threshold, not a universal statistical guarantee.
cards.statement: A false-alarm-rate threshold of two per year was imposed in each of the four search pipelines to identify candidate gravitational wave events, resulting in an expected contamination fraction of less than 10%.

cards.design_implication: Research designs involving ambiguous compact binary candidates should treat classification based on mass and spin data as provisional, acknowledging that ambiguity exists in this data stream.
does_not_establish: Alternative methods that might resolve these ambiguities
The total number of such ambiguous events in the broader universe
cards.evidence_excerpt: For the latter group, we are unable to determine the nature based on estimates of the component masses and spins from gravitational wave data alone.
limitations: This boundary applies to the 'latter group' of events in this catalog where identification was ambiguous.
It restricts the interpretation of gravitational wave parameter estimates for these specific cases.
cards.statement: For events whose components could not be unambiguously identified as black holes or neutron stars, the nature cannot be determined based solely on estimates of the component masses and spins from gravitational wave data.
